rule: By video, never by frame. Sort the 20 VISEM-Tracking videos ascending by class-0 boxes per labelled frame (ties by numeric id), cut into 5 consecutive groups of 4, and hold out from each group the video whose sha256('spiketrack-lora-split-v1:<id>') hex digest is smallest. The other 15 train. No RNG: tools/reference/make_visem_split.py regenerates this file.

fixture_videos.leakage: None, so no video is excluded from held-out. Backbone fixtures (22, 47, 82), the detector detail fixture (22), the D3 gate (20 frames cycling through all 20 videos) and the detect_track reference (11) all run the BASE model and check Rust against PyTorch parity; they never train. The LoRA adapter is evaluated only on the held-out videos' frames.
